title: How to Register Your Business with the CAC Online in Nigeria
excerpt: Ready to legitimize your hustle? Learn the exact process of registering your Business Name with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) online in Nigeria without hiring expensive lawyers.
keywords: how to register business in nigeria

sections.content: Operating an unregistered business in Nigeria limits your growth potential. Without official registration, you cannot open a corporate bank account, apply for government grants, secure commercial bank loans, or build trust with international clients. Registering your Business Name with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) is the first and most important step toward building a legitimate, trustworthy brand. Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA 2020), the federal government mandates that any individual or entity carrying out commercial activities under a name other than their true surname must register that name, protecting consumers and operators alike.

In the past, CAC registration required hiring lawyers or chartered secretaries, leading to high fees. Today, the CAC has fully digitized the process, allowing citizens to register via the Pre-CAC online portal. However, navigating this portal can be confusing. Formatting errors, name clashes, or incorrect documents can trigger queries that delay your registration for months. This guide breaks down the differences in business structures, details the registration steps, and shows you how to use a trusted accredited agency to handle it for you, ensuring a seamless experience.

Building a brand in Nigeria requires a solid legal foundation. When you present an official CAC certificate and a Tax Identification Number (TIN) to partners, it changes how your business is perceived. It moves you from a casual side-hustle to a corporate entity, opening doors to vendor contracts, merchant payment portals, and official business listings. Protecting your business name early also ensures that no one else can register it and claim your hard-earned brand equity, securing your future expansion plans, allowing you to establish a strong presence in the market.

Furthermore, many online payment gateways (like Paystack, Flutterwave, and Monnify) require a CAC certificate to upgrade your merchant account from a starter profile to a business profile. Unregistered starter profiles are limited on how much cash they can receive daily and are subject to immediate payout blocks if their transactions spike. Registering early removes these caps, letting your payment flows run continuously, preventing unexpected account holds, safeguarding your customer transactions, giving you full control of corporate cash flows, enabling automated settlement channels.

Our guide details these legal and administrative steps in clear, simple terms that any entrepreneur can understand. Whether you run a retail shop, a digital reselling hub, a fashion house, or a local cybercafe, registering your business correctly ensures you avoid legal friction and can access corporate financial instruments easily, helping you scale your business beyond micro-limits, ensuring you remain in business for the long haul, securing your assets from third-party liabilities.

sections.content: Business Name (Sole Proprietorship) vs. Private Limited Company (LTD)
Before you begin registration, you must choose the right business structure. The CAC offers different categories depending on your scale and corporate goals:

A Business Name (Enterprise / Sole Proprietorship) is the simplest and cheapest form of registration. Legally, you and the business are the same entity. The business profits are taxed as your personal income, and you are personally liable for any debts the business incurs. This structure is ideal for freelancers, small retail shops, data resellers, and micro-startups due to its low setup costs and minimal filing requirements. It allows you to operate under a distinct name without complex corporate tax rules, saving you from heavy compliance audits, keeping your business running without high accountant fees, allowing you to retain the maximum value from your trading activities.

A Private Limited Company (LTD) is a more complex structure that creates a separate legal entity. The company can own properties, sue, and be sued. The personal assets of the shareholders are protected by limited liability if the business faces financial issues. An LTD requires at least one director and shareholder, and has higher setup costs and tax filing rules. It is the best choice if you plan to seek venture capital or partner with institutional investors, as it provides a structured share capital allocation, making it easy to onboard partners, ensuring credibility, protecting directors from financial liability.
Requirements for Business Name Registration
Before launching the online application, gather these documents and details to ensure a smooth application process:

items: Two Proposed Business Names: You must submit two names in order of preference (e.g. 'Apex Digital Services' as primary, and 'Apex Cyber Hub' as backup) in case one is already in use.
National Identification Number (NIN): A valid NIN is required to verify your identity.
Passport Photograph: A clear, color passport photo with a plain background.
Scanned Signature: Sign your name on a plain white sheet of paper, scan it, or take a clear photo in good lighting.
Addresses: Provide the physical residential address of the proprietor and the official business location (these can be the same).

sections.content: Step-by-Step Guide to DIY CAC Online Registration
If you decide to register the business yourself, follow this step-by-step process on the official portal:

steps.title: Create a Public User Account
steps.content: Go to pre.cac.gov.ng. Click 'Register' and create an account by verifying your NIN, inputting your email, and setting a password.

steps.title: Submit Name Reservation
steps.content: Log in, click on 'New Name Reservation', fill in the name options, select your business type, and pay the ₦500 reservation fee via Remita. The CAC team will review and approve or reject the name within 24 to 72 hours.

steps.title: Complete Registration Forms
steps.content: Once your name is approved, go to 'Action' and click 'Start Registration'. Fill in your business objectives, proprietor details, address, and upload your passport and signature.

steps.title: Pay the Registration Fee
steps.content: Pay the statutory registration fee of ₦10,000 via Remita on the portal.

steps.title: Download the Certificate
steps.content: The CAC officers will review your documents. If there are no errors, your application will be approved, and you can download your official Certificate of Registration, Status Report, and TIN PDF.

sections.content: Filing Annual Returns: Keeping Your Business Active

Getting your certificate is not the end of the process. Under CAMA 2020 guidelines, every registered business in Nigeria must file an **Annual Return** with the CAC every year. Annual returns are not tax payments; they are a statutory filing to notify the CAC that your business is still active. Filing is due by June 30th of each year, starting the year after registration. Failing to file results in a daily penalty fee, and if left unpaid, the CAC can flag your business status as 'Inactive' or strike it off the national register, blocking you from opening bank accounts or using payment portals, resulting in business delays, locking your assets, shutting down your corporate lines.

sections.content: Common Mistakes that Trigger CAC Rejections & Queries

items: Name Arrangement Mismatch: If your submitted name does not match the spelling on your NIN profile, the CAC will reject the name reservation.
Prohibited Words: Do not use restricted words like 'National', 'Federal', 'Government', 'Cooperative', or 'Chamber of Commerce' without official approvals, as they are reserved for state bodies.

Vague Business Objectives: Listing your business nature as 'General Contract' or 'Trading' is too vague. State clearly what you do (e.g. 'Vending of telecommunication products, bill payments, and web design services').

sections.content: Understanding Post-incorporation Filings and Changes

Over time, your business needs may change. You might relocate your business office, add new partners, change directors, or upgrade your business name from a Sole Proprietorship to a Private Limited Company. These alterations are managed through the CAC Post-incorporation portal. Filing these changes requires paying statutory fees and uploading board resolutions. Keeping your records updated ensures your bank profiles remain active and matches the NIBSS validation registries, preventing transaction limits, protecting your corporate name.
Tax Compliance and Obtaining Your VAT Certificate

Once your business is registered, you should set up tax compliance channels. The Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) requires registered businesses to file tax returns. If you sell physical goods or services subject to Value Added Tax (VAT), you should register on the FIRS portal to generate your VAT number. Having a complete tax profile is a legal requirement for bidding for corporate vendor tenders, ensuring your business stays clean and legally protected under federal laws, keeping your trade books 100% compliant, protecting you from sudden audits.
Resolving Registration Name Conflicts and Duplicates

Sometimes, the CAC rejects your name reservation because it is similar to an already registered brand. For instance, if 'Apex Tech Services' exists, registering 'Apex Tech Hub' will be flagged. To resolve this, do a free search on the public search index (publicsearch.cac.gov.ng) before choosing a name. Choosing a unique, highly specific name ensures you pass reservation on the first attempt, saving name reservation fees, preventing duplicate filings, making the setup stress-free.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

items: How long does CAC registration take? If there are no queries, name reservation takes 1-3 days, and the final certificate generation takes about 1-2 weeks.
Do I need a TIN (Tax Identification Number) to register? No. Once your CAC certificate is approved and generated, the government will automatically assign and print a TIN on your certificate.
Can a minor register a business in Nigeria? No, you must be at least 18 years old to register a business, unless two other directors who are adults are included in the application.
What is the funding fee on Ufriends IT? Ufriends IT charges a simple 1% fee on automated virtual bank transfers, with funds crediting in under 15 seconds.
Can I register an LTD company on Ufriends? Yes, you can submit both Business Name (Sole Proprietorship) and Limited Liability Company (LTD) requests on the dashboard.
How do I download my approved certificate? Once approved, the PDF files are uploaded to your Ufriends dashboard. You can download and print them on standard cardboard paper.
What happens if my business name is rejected? If the CAC rejections your proposed name during name reservation, you must submit new names and pay another name reservation fee.
Is the physical CAC certificate still issued? No, the CAC now issues electronic certificates (e-certificates) containing a QR code for instant bank verification.
How do I open a bank account after registration? Visit any commercial bank with your CAC certificate, status report, TIN, and valid ID card, and fill out a corporate account opening form.
Can I change my business address later? Yes, you can file a 'Notice of Change of Registered Address' form on the post-incorporation portal, paying a filing fee.
Can I add partners to a Business Name? Yes, a Business Name can have multiple partners (proprietors) registered under the same business.
